title: Keyboard users lose their place when a tool closes: after closing the palette with Escape…
request:
# Keyboard users lose their place when a tool closes: after closing the palette with Escape…

This request comes from a problem found while building "Keep the footer, and make its toggle behave the same as the sidebar's Ctrl+B… (and 4 more)" (run 20261125-202512) that could not be fixed there. The rest of that feature was kept; this is what was left.

## What this is about

Keyboard users lose their place when a tool closes: after closing the palette with Escape focus drops to <body>, and closing the git drawer leaves focus on the hidden Close button. This fails the revision's accessibility requirement that the palette and every hide control 'return focus to a sensible place when a tool closes' (and the keyboard check 'closes the palette with Escape ... with visible focus at each step'). Capture the focused element when the palette/drawer opens and restore it on close (or move focus to a named control such as the palette trigger or the Changes/History control).

## What was found

- REV-3, found by reviewer, about USR-006
- Where: src/features/command-palette/CommandPalette.tsx:43

What was seen:

The Escape handler closes the palette with onClose() (line 43) and choose() closes it with onClose() (line 57); the component unmounts without saving or restoring document.activeElement. A jsdom probe that renders the palette exactly as App does (open -> input focused -> Escape -> unmount) leaves document.activeElement as BODY. The same gap exists for the git drawer hide control: App.tsx:615-617 wraps GitDrawer in <div hidden={gitTab === null}> and its onClose is () => setGitTab(null), so the focused Close button is hidden with no focus hand-off. The only .focus() calls in src are open-time focus (CommandPalette.tsx:36, Dialog.tsx:19); there is no focus restore anywhere.

## What was tried

The developer was given 6 revision round(s) for the problems of that feature and this one was still open.
